newsitem.title: CANADA: Canbra Foods head confused by stock rise.
newsitem.headline: Canbra Foods head confused by stock rise.

text.p: A C$3 a share gain in Canbra Foods Ltd stock on the Toronto Stock Exchange by midday Wednesday after Tuesday's news of an increase in a takeover bid has the canola crusher's president confused.

"If this goes through, those people will receive C$22.63 for their shares and they'll no longer own Canbra so dividend potential will be lost when they tender those shares, that's what confuses me," Canbra Foods Ltd president Larry McNamara told Reuters in a phone interview.
Canbra shares traded at C$22.50 a share at 1120 EST/1620 GMT in volume of 50,320 after Tuesday's close at C$19.50.

"If you say they're trying to acquire shares to prevent this from happening, then I think the share value would probably slip down to the realistic levels it was trading at before in the C$14 range. There's a lot of risk on that side if it doesn't go through," McNamara added.
Minority shareholders' votes will be counted December 16 on Tuesday's amended takeover proposal, he said.
Hartford Securities, a wholly owned unit of Pocklington Financial (1996) Corp, raised its offer to minority shareholders by C$1.63 on Tuesday to a total of C$22.63.
A share price of C$22.50 means little room for commission.

"The arbitrage opportunity's pretty small. Obviously the stock market thinks its a good idea because the share price quickly went to the point of equilibrium," Scotia McLeod commodity analyst Rob Gigiel said.
Canbra is one of five canola seed crushers in Canada.
Canola is an oilseed used in margarine and cooking oil. It is favored in premium markets like Japan because it has the lowest saturated fat content of any of the world's oilseeds.
"They buy canola seed and produce margarine at the other end and that's what makes them profitable," Linnco Futures Group commodity analyst Rob Diziak said.

Canola crushing profit margins recovered from the year's low in July just before harvest but has since decline with the January Winnipeg Commodity Exchange futures crush margin at rising to -39.83 from -44.04 Monday, based on January Chicago Board of Trade soyoil and soybean meal futures.
Canbra is one of the few fully integrated Canadian canola processors that packages its final product on site.
One market participant said Pocklington's offer of a 16 percent premium over Tuesday's close at C$19.50 seemed "reasonable" to buy out minority share holders.
If approved, the buyout will occur Dec 18, McNamara said.
